_readme: Coverage policy for the UI-language / native-source health audit.
The app ships 26 UI languages (src/services/i18n.ts SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES) but a
feed only reaches a user whose UI language matches its `lang` tag, or that
carries `strategicDefault` (src/services/feed-language.ts). An untagged feed is
universal — in practice English-language journalism. So a UI language with zero
`lang`-tagged sources ships a fully translated interface over a news pane that
contains no journalism written in that language.
universalPoolLanguage: the language the UNTAGGED pool is written in. Those
feeds carry no `lang`, reach every locale, and are the bulk of both catalogs,
so this one language is exempt from the native-source floor and the digest
parity check — measuring it by `lang`-tagged count alone would report a
catalog of hundreds of English sources as having none.
floors: minimum NATIVE (lang-tagged) client sources required per UI language.
Unlisted languages default to 1. These are a RATCHET, not a target: they lock
in today's coverage so it cannot silently regress. Raise a floor as sources land.
zeroNativeAllowlist: UI languages that currently have ZERO native sources,
with a documented reason. The audit fails BOTH ways — a language drops to zero
without being listed here (new gap), or a listed language gains native coverage
and the entry is not removed (stale allowlist). Shrink this list as coverage lands.
digestBlindAllowlist: UI languages whose native sources exist client-side but
never reach the server digest catalog (server/worldmonitor/news/v1/_feeds.ts),
so no AI brief is ever built from journalism in that language. Same two-way
ratchet as zeroNativeAllowlist.

zeroNativeAllowlist.fa: Zero fa sources client-side. The server digest catalog carries BBC Persian, so the asymmetry runs the OTHER way here: the brief can ingest Persian journalism the news pane can never show. Mirror BBC Persian into src/config/feeds.ts to clear this.

digestBlindAllowlist.ar: Asharq News is the only ar source and it is client-only. Arabic is ~400M speakers with a fully translated RTL interface, so this is the widest gap in the catalog.
digestBlindAllowlist.pt: O Globo, Folha de S.Paulo and Brasil Paralelo are all client-only. Brazil is a Tier-1 commodity and geopolitical subject the briefs currently reason about using English coverage only.
